# Host API by surface

<!-- Generated by config/scripts/generate-plugin-authoring-skill-references.mjs. Do not edit. -->

Host API 1.9 (`"pluginApi": 1`). Call `host.call(method, params, { signal })`; a surface not listed for a method gets `not_permitted`. Params are strict: a field this Orca does not know is refused with `invalid_params`, so check `host.has(method)` or `api.minor` before using a method newer than your `engines.orca` floor. Each call also needs the manifest capability and the user's approval.

## Methods per surface

- Worker (`trusted-worker`, `main`): `orca` passed to `activate(orca)`: `workspace.readContext`, `terminal.sendText`, `notifications.show`, `storage.get`, `storage.set`, `storage.delete`, `storage.keys`, `secrets.get`, `secrets.set`, `secrets.delete`, `secrets.protection`, `settings.get`, `settings.set`, `agents.list`, `statusBar.update`, `appearance.read`, `appearance.apply`, `workspace.list`, `project.list`, `workspace.open`, `workspace.rename`, `terminal.create`, `terminal.read`, `agent.launch`, `editor.open`, `commands.run`, `terminal.list`, `terminal.focus`, `terminal.close`, `workspace.create`, `agent.resume`, `automation.list`, `automation.create`, `automation.update`, `automation.delete`, `agent.listSessions`, `editor.readTypography`
- Panel: global `orca` in an HTML panel; `host` imported from `orca` in a components panel: `workspace.readContext`, `notifications.show`, `storage.get`, `storage.set`, `storage.delete`, `storage.keys`, `secrets.get`, `secrets.set`, `secrets.delete`, `secrets.protection`, `settings.get`, `settings.set`, `shell.openExternal`, `files.saveAs`, `plugin.request`, `agents.list`, `events.subscribe`, `editor.readTypography`
- Custom editor: global `orca` in the editor frame: `workspace.readContext`, `notifications.show`, `storage.get`, `storage.set`, `storage.delete`, `storage.keys`, `secrets.get`, `secrets.set`, `secrets.delete`, `secrets.protection`, `settings.get`, `settings.set`, `shell.openExternal`, `files.saveAs`, `plugin.request`, `agents.list`, `events.subscribe`, `editor.readTypography`

## Worker API (`import type { OrcaWorkerApi } from 'orca/worker'`)

- `api: HostApiVersion`
- `commands.register(commandId: string, handler: (args: unknown, context: CommandContext) => unknown)`: A string result is shown as-is in Orca; anything else as JSON.
- `events.on(event: E, handler: (payload: PluginEvents[E]) => void | Promise<void>)`: Only events listed in the manifest's `contributes.events` arrive.
- `hooks.on(hook: H, handler: HookHandler<H>)`: Only hooks listed in `contributes.hooks` run. Return `next(event)` to go on (with the fields the hook allows changed), a result such as `{ deny: reason }` to stop, or nothing to pass. Plugins run in turn, then Orca acts; past 2 s, or on a throw, Orca carries on as if this plugin passed and logs it.
- `host: HostApi<'worker'>`
- `panels: PanelsApi`: This plugin's panels and custom editors.
- `storage: StorageApi`: Same store as panels' `storage` (`storage:own`); `onDidChange` hears their writes too.
- `settings: SettingsApi`: `settings:own`; `onDidChange` also hears the person changing them in Settings.
- `secrets: SecretsApi`: `secrets:own`.
- `grantedCapabilities: readonly string[]`: Consented capability kinds; informational, the host re-checks every call.
- `log(message: string)`: Lands in `orca plugin logs`.

## Frame API (global `orca`, also `window.orca`, in HTML panels and custom editors)

- `api: HostApiVersion`
- `host: HostApi<'panel' | 'editor'>`
- `on(event: E, handler: (payload: FrameEvents[E]) => unknown)`
- `locale: string`: Orca's UI language as a BCP-47 tag.
- `plugin: PluginBridgeApi`: Your plugin's own worker: `request` its handlers, hear what it `post`s.
- `storage: StorageApi`: The plugin's own storage, the same its worker uses (`storage:own`).
- `settings: SettingsApi`: The plugin's settings, declared ones with their defaults (`settings:own`).
- `secrets: SecretsApi`: The plugin's encrypted secrets (`secrets:own`).
- `shell.openExternal(url: string)`: `reason`: the person cancelled, or Orca's window was hidden so nobody could confirm.
- `files.saveAs(options: SaveAsOptions)`: Desktop isolated frames only; `cancelled` when the person closes the dialog.
- `document?: EditorDocumentApi`: Custom editors only. Orca keeps no undo history for them: Cmd/Ctrl+Z reaches the frame.
- `document.get()`: The latest document, with your accepted edits' content at the same version.
- `document.onDidChange(handler: (document: EditorDocument) => void)`: Replays the current document, then each one Orca sends when the file changes outside.
- `document.applyEdit(edit: EditorEdit)`: Rejects with `conflict`, `too_large` or `not_permitted` (read-only).
- `document.session(options?: EditorSessionOptions<T>)`: Document sync in one call; resolves once theme, locale and the first document are in.

## Theme variables in frames

HTML panels and custom editors get these CSS variables from Orca's active theme, plus a `light` or `dark` class on `<html>`. A theme change updates them in place and emits `theme` (`orca.on('theme', ...)`); the frame is not reloaded. Style from them, not fixed colours.

- `--orca-background`: App canvas
- `--orca-foreground`: Body text
- `--orca-card`: Cards and panels
- `--orca-card-foreground`: Text on `--orca-card`
- `--orca-popover`: Menus, popovers and dialogs
- `--orca-popover-foreground`: Text on `--orca-popover`
- `--orca-primary`: Primary buttons
- `--orca-primary-foreground`: Text on `--orca-primary`
- `--orca-secondary`: Secondary buttons
- `--orca-secondary-foreground`: Text on `--orca-secondary`
- `--orca-muted`: Quiet fills
- `--orca-muted-foreground`: Secondary text
- `--orca-accent`: Hover and selected fills
- `--orca-accent-foreground`: Text on `--orca-accent`
- `--orca-destructive`
- `--orca-destructive-foreground`
- `--orca-border`: Borders and separators
- `--orca-input`: Input borders
- `--orca-ring`: Focus rings
- `--orca-radius`: Corner radius of cards and controls

## Methods

- `workspace.readContext` (capability `workspace:read`; worker, panel, editor; since 1.0): Id, branch, name and terminal ids of the focused workspace, or null when none is focused.
  `(params?: {}) => { workspaceId?: string; branch: string; displayName: string; terminals: { id: string; title?: string }[] } | null`
- `terminal.sendText` (capability `terminal:send`; worker; since 1.0): Types text into one terminal named by id, optionally pressing Enter.
  `(params: { terminalId: string; text: string; enter?: boolean }) => { accepted: boolean }`
- `notifications.show` (capability `notifications:show`; worker, panel, editor; since 1.0): Shows a desktop notification.
  `(params: { title: string; body?: string }) => { delivered: boolean }`
- `storage.get` (capability `storage:own`; worker, panel, editor; since 1.0): Reads a JSON value from the plugin's private store; null when absent.
  `(params: { key: string }) => { value: JSON }`
- `storage.set` (capability `storage:own`; worker, panel, editor; since 1.0): Writes a JSON value to the plugin's private store.
  `(params: { key: string; value: JSON }) => { ok: true }`
- `storage.delete` (capability `storage:own`; worker, panel, editor; since 1.0): Removes a key from the plugin's private store.
  `(params: { key: string }) => { ok: true }`
- `storage.keys` (capability `storage:own`; worker, panel, editor; since 1.0): Lists the keys in the plugin's private store.
  `(params?: {}) => { keys: string[] }`
- `secrets.get` (capability `secrets:own`; worker, panel, editor; since 1.0): Reads a secret from the plugin's encrypted secrets file; null when absent.
  `(params: { key: string }) => { value: string | null }`
- `secrets.set` (capability `secrets:own`; worker, panel, editor; since 1.0): Stores a secret in the plugin's encrypted secrets file.
  `(params: { key: string; value: string }) => { ok: true }`
- `secrets.delete` (capability `secrets:own`; worker, panel, editor; since 1.0): Removes a secret from the plugin's encrypted secrets file.
  `(params: { key: string }) => { ok: true }`
- `secrets.protection` (capability `secrets:own`; worker, panel, editor; since 1.1): How secrets are protected at rest: `os-keyring`, or `unavailable` (no OS key store, or Linux `basic_text`), where `secrets.set` fails.
  `(params?: {}) => { status: "os-keyring" | "unavailable" }`
- `settings.get` (capability `settings:own`; worker, panel, editor; since 1.0): Reads every setting the plugin owns.
  `(params?: {}) => { settings: Record<string, JSON> }`
- `settings.set` (capability `settings:own`; worker, panel, editor; since 1.0): Writes one setting the plugin owns.
  `(params: { key: string; value: JSON }) => { ok: true }`
- `shell.openExternal` (no capability; panel, editor; since 1.1; needs a user gesture): Opens an http:, https: or mailto: URL in the default browser. Needs a click or key press in the frame; desktop app only. Orca asks the person before an http(s) host the plugin was not allowed; `opened` is false if they cancel.
  `(params: { url: string }) => { opened: boolean; reason?: "cancelled" | "consent-unavailable" }`
- `files.saveAs` (no capability; panel, editor; since 1.1; needs a user gesture): Offers data (a string or ArrayBuffer, up to 64 MiB) in Orca's save dialog; the plugin never learns the path. Needs a click or key press in the frame; desktop app only.
  `(params: { suggestedName?: string; mimeType?: string; data: string | ArrayBuffer }) => { status: "saved" | "cancelled" }`
- `plugin.request` (no capability; panel, editor; since 1.2): Asks the plugin's own worker to run the handler it registered with `orca.panels.handle(name)`, starting the worker if needed; resolves with what the handler returned. `unknown_method` when no handler has that name.
  `(params: { name: string; input?: JSON; timeoutMs?: number }) => { output: JSON }`
- `agents.list` (capability `agent:read`; worker, panel, editor; since 1.2): The agents in the focused workspace: their terminal, title, agent kind, status, session and dispatched task. `agent.status.changed` reports each change after.
  `(params?: {}) => { agents: { terminalId: string | null; title: string | null; agent: string | null; state: "working" | "blocked" | "waiting" | "done"; stateStartedAt: number; sessionId?: string | null; task?: { title: string } | null }[] }`
- `events.subscribe` (no capability; panel, editor; since 1.2): Delivers a workspace, agent or editor event to this panel as `orca.on(event)`; needs the event's read capability, when it has one. The frame APIs call it for you.
  `(params: { event: "workspace.created" | "workspace.removed" | "agent.status.changed" | "workspace.changed" | "editor.typography.changed" }) => { ok: true }`
- `statusBar.update` (no capability; worker; since 1.2): Changes one of the plugin's `contributes.statusBarItems` (named by `id`): fields given replace their current value, `visible: false` hides it. Desktop app only; lasts until Orca restarts, and is hidden while the plugin is disabled. A plugin with `main` and status bar items has its worker started when it is enabled and kept running while it stays enabled, so a worker can poll and update its items without an event or a hook.
  `(params: { id: string; text?: string; icon?: "activity" | "bar-chart-3" | "bell" | "blocks" | "book" | "bot" | "bug" | "calendar" | "cloud" | "code" | "database" | "file-text" | "flag" | "folder" | "gauge" | "globe" | "hammer" | "layers" | "lightbulb" | "package" | "plug" | "puzzle" | "rocket" | "star" | "terminal" | "wrench" | "zap" | "add" | "remove" | "delete" | "edit" | "refresh" | "search" | "settings" | "check" | "close" | "info" | "warning" | "error" | "open-external" | "copy" | "download" | "upload" | "play" | "pause" | "stop" | "more" | "expand" | "collapse" | "next" | "filter" | "branch" | "file" | "agent" | "link"; tone?: "neutral" | "accent" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"; tooltip?: string; visible?: boolean }) => { ok: true }`
- `appearance.read` (capability `appearance:write`; worker; since 1.4): Reads the current desktop appearance revision for a conditional update.
  `(params?: {}) => { revision: string }`
- `appearance.apply` (capability `appearance:write`; worker; since 1.4): Publishes owned app/editor and terminal colors and selects them in the desktop. Returns publication, not renderer acknowledgement.
  `(params: { expectedRevision: string; app: string; terminal: string }) => { revision: string; themeId: string; mode: "dark" | "light"; delivery: "published" }`
- `workspace.list` (capability `workspace:read`; worker; since 1.3): Lists every workspace, Git worktrees and folders, on every host Orca reaches; `includeStatus` (host API 1.7) adds each one's agent status. `hostId` is the host a row records (`local`, `ssh:…`, `runtime:…`), or null when it records none, as for a project-group folder on this machine.
  `(params?: { includeStatus?: boolean }) => { workspaces: { id: string; kind: "worktree" | "folder"; name: string; project?: string | null; projectId?: string | null; path: string; branch: string | null; hostId: string | null; status?: { state: "working" | "permission" | "done" | "active" | "inactive"; unread: boolean; terminalCount: number; lastActivityAt: number | null } }[]; truncated: boolean; statusTruncated?: boolean }`
- `project.list` (capability `workspace:read`; worker; since 1.7): Lists your projects (repositories and folders) on every host; `id` is what `workspace.list` rows name as `projectId`. `hostId` is always named: `local`, `ssh:…` or `runtime:…`.
  `(params?: {}) => { projects: { id: string; name: string; kind: "git" | "folder"; hostId: string | null; path: string }[]; truncated: boolean }`
- `workspace.open` (capability `workspace:write`; worker; since 1.3): Shows a workspace in Orca, as clicking it in the sidebar does; a folder workspace needs the desktop app.
  `(params: { workspaceId: string }) => { opened: true }`
- `workspace.rename` (capability `workspace:write`; worker; since 1.5): Renames a workspace in Orca's sidebar, as renaming it by hand does; the name stays until it is renamed again.
  `(params: { workspaceId: string; name: string }) => { name: string }`
- `terminal.create` (capability `terminal:send`; worker; since 1.3): Opens a terminal in a workspace, optionally running a command, in the background.
  `(params: { workspaceId: string; title?: string; command?: string }) => { terminalId: string }`
- `terminal.read` (capability `terminal:read`; worker; since 1.3): Reads a terminal's newest output as plain text, at most 2000 lines.
  `(params: { terminalId: string; maxLines?: number }) => { lines: string[]; truncated: boolean }`
- `agent.launch` (capability `agent:launch`; worker; since 1.3): Starts an agent's CLI in a new terminal of a workspace, in the background, and returns as soon as it starts; a `prompt` is sent once the agent is ready.
  `(params: { workspaceId: string; agent: string; prompt?: string }) => { terminalId: string }`
- `editor.open` (capability `workspace:write`; worker; since 1.3): Opens a file of a workspace in an editor tab of Orca's window; desktop app only. `workspace.open` shows the workspace.
  `(params: { workspaceId: string; path: string }) => { opened: true }`
- `commands.run` (capability `workspace:write`; worker; since 1.3): Runs one of Orca's built-in actions in its window, never a plugin's replacement of it; desktop app only.
  `(params: { action: "worktree.history.back" | "worktree.history.forward" | "sidebar.left.toggle" | "sidebar.sleepingWorkspaces.toggle" | "floatingWorkspace.maximize" | "tab.rename" | "workspace.rename" | "workspace.openBoard" | "view.tasks" | "sidebar.right.toggle" | "sidebar.explorer.toggle" | "sidebar.search.toggle" | "sidebar.sourceControl.toggle" | "sidebar.checks.toggle" | "sidebar.ports.toggle" }) => { ran: true }`
- `terminal.list` (capability `workspace:read`; worker; since 1.7): Lists a workspace's terminals, at most 50; `workspace.readContext` lists the focused one's.
  `(params: { workspaceId: string }) => { terminals: { id: string; title?: string }[]; truncated: boolean }`
- `terminal.focus` (capability `workspace:write`; worker; since 1.7): Shows any terminal's workspace and focuses its pane, as clicking it does; desktop app only. `focused` is false when a newer focus request won or the window did not move to it.
  `(params: { terminalId: string }) => { focused: boolean }`
- `terminal.close` (capability `terminal:send`; worker; since 1.7): Closes a terminal of the focused workspace, or one this plugin opened (`terminal.create`, `agent.launch`), stopping what runs in it (local or SSH); closing its last pane closes the tab. Any other terminal is refused with `action_failed`. A plugin keeps its terminals until it is disabled or removed.
  `(params: { terminalId: string }) => { closed: true }`
- `workspace.create` (capability `workspace:create`; `agent` also needs `agent:launch`; worker; since 1.8): Creates a workspace (a new branch and worktree) in a Git project, local or SSH, and returns its id; with `agent`, starts that agent there once setup has run, in the background unless `open`; if the agent fails after the workspace exists, the error names its id. Orca's workspace-create and agent hooks run as for any create.
  `(params: { projectId: string; hostId?: string; name?: string; baseBranch?: string; agent?: string; prompt?: string; setup?: "skip"; open?: boolean }) => { workspaceId: string; terminalId?: string }`
- `agent.resume` (capability `agent:launch`; worker; since 1.8): Resumes an agent's earlier session by its `sessionId` in a new terminal of a workspace, in the background; `started` is false when an Orca terminal already runs it. From host API 1.9, a session no Orca pane runs that Agent Session History lists on this computer (among the workspace's own sessions and the 200 newest) is prepared and started as Orca's own Resume does, in the agent account Orca would pick; only `agent:launch` is needed, since the plugin must already know the id. Other sessions, and workspaces on another host, resume by id. In WSL it uses the distro's default agent account, as `agent.launch` does.
  `(params: { workspaceId: string; agent: "claude" | "codebuddy" | "codex" | "qoder" | "qoder-cn" | "qwen-code" | "gemini" | "antigravity" | "opencode" | "opencode2" | "pi" | "mimo-code" | "droid" | "grok" | "devin" | "omp" | "prime-agent" | "copilot" | "cursor" | "kimi" | "muse" | "zcode" | "dsh" | "jcode" | "kiro" | "hermes"; sessionId: string }) => { terminalId: string; started: boolean }`
- `automation.list` (capability `automation:read`; worker; since 1.8): Lists the automations this Orca schedules, at most 200, with each one's prompt cut to 4096 characters.
  `(params?: {}) => { automations: { id: string; name: string; agent: string; prompt: string; promptTruncated: boolean; projectId: string | null; hostId: string | null; workspaceId: string | null; workspaceMode: "existing" | "new-per-run"; schedule: string | null; timezone: string; enabled: boolean; nextRunAt: number | null; lastRunAt: number | null; createdByThisPlugin: boolean }[]; truncated: boolean }`
- `automation.create` (capability `automation:write`; worker; since 1.8): Creates an automation that starts `agent` with `prompt` on `schedule`, even when the plugin is not running, with the person's settings for that agent; Orca's Automations page shows it as created by the plugin.
  `(params: { name: string; prompt: string; agent: string; projectId?: string; hostId?: string; workspaceId?: string; schedule: string; timezone?: string; enabled?: boolean; creationKey?: string }) => { automationId: string }`
- `automation.update` (capability `automation:write`; worker; since 1.8): Changes an automation's name, prompt, schedule, time zone or whether it is enabled. Orca first asks the person about an automation this plugin did not create (or created before it was removed or disabled); if they decline or cannot be asked, or it changes while they are asked, nothing changes and `reason` says why. Orca also asks before a new prompt or schedule, or resuming, for any automation whose runs use extra agent settings the person chose.
  `(params: { automationId: string; name?: string; prompt?: string; schedule?: string; timezone?: string; enabled?: boolean }) => { updated: boolean; reason?: "cancelled" | "consent-unavailable" | "changed" }`
- `automation.delete` (capability `automation:write`; worker; since 1.8): Deletes an automation. Orca first asks the person about an automation this plugin did not create (or created before it was removed or disabled); if they decline or cannot be asked, or it changes while they are asked, nothing changes and `reason` says why.
  `(params: { automationId: string }) => { deleted: boolean; reason?: "cancelled" | "consent-unavailable" | "changed" }`
- `agent.listSessions` (capability `history:read`; worker; since 1.9): Past agent sessions in Orca's Agent Session History on this computer (WSL distributions included on Windows), newest first: title, agent, workspace, branch, times, message and token counts, and whether an Orca terminal here runs it. Leaves out Antigravity IDE conversations and subagent transcripts, and never gives the conversation or file paths, though a title can be the start of its first message. `agent.resume` resumes one by its `sessionId`, for agents that resume by id.
  `(params?: { workspaceId?: string; limit?: number }) => { sessions: { sessionId: string; agent: string; title: string; workspaceId: string | null; hostId: string; branch: string | null; createdAt: number | null; updatedAt: number; messageCount: number; totalTokens: number; running: boolean }[]; truncated: boolean }`
- `editor.readTypography` (no capability; worker, panel, editor; since 1.6): The font family, size, weight, line height, ligatures, word wrap and minimap Orca's file editor uses now, editor zoom included. `editor.typography.changed` reports each change after.
  `(params?: {}) => { fontFamily: string; cssFontFamily: string; fontSize: number; fontWeight: string; lineHeight: number; fontLigatures: boolean; wordWrap: "on" | "off"; minimap: boolean }`

## Hooks

List each in `contributes.hooks` (`{ "event", "onError"? }`; `main` and `trusted-worker`) and handle it with `orca.hooks.on(event, (event, next) => ...)`. Return `next(event)` (or nothing) to go on, or the stop result. Plugins run in turn, 2 s each; a throw, timeout or crash passes unless the entry says `"onError": "deny"`. Decide first: an awaited call before you return (a notification, say) can fail or time out and turn your deny into a pass.

- `terminal.send` (since 1.4.248): Text Orca, the CLI or a plugin is about to send to a terminal. A person typing (on the desktop, a phone or a paired client) is never hooked, and prompts Orca submits to an agent take `agent.prompt.before` instead. Writes to one terminal stay in order while a hook decides. Rewrite `text` or `enter` with `next`, or return `{ deny }` to refuse the send.
  event `{ terminalId: string; text: string; enter: boolean; inputKind: "driving" | "orchestration" | "launch" }`; `next` may change `text`, `enter`; stop with `{ deny: string }`
- `workspace.create.before` (since 1.4.248): A worktree or folder workspace is about to be created. Change `name`, `branch` or `base` with `next`, or return `{ deny }` to refuse it.
  event `{ kind: "worktree" | "folder"; projectId: string; name: string; branch?: string; base?: string }`; `next` may change `name`, `branch`, `base`; stop with `{ deny: string }`
- `workspace.create.after` (since 1.4.248): A worktree or folder workspace was created. Observe only: Orca does not wait for it, and results are ignored.
  event `{ workspaceId: string; kind: "worktree" | "folder"; path: string; branch: string }`; `next` may change nothing; stop with nothing (observe only)
- `agent.launch.before` (since 1.4.248): Orca is about to start an agent CLI in a terminal, from any launcher (new tab, workspace create, CLI, automation, orchestration). Change `command` or add `env` with `next`, or return `{ deny }` to refuse the launch. Restores of saved sessions are not hooked.
  event `{ agent: string; workspaceId: string | null; workspaceKind: "worktree" | "folder" | null; terminalId?: string; command: string; env: Record<string, string> }`; `next` may change `command`, `env`; stop with `{ deny: string }`
- `agent.prompt.before` (since 1.4.248): Orca is about to submit a prompt to an agent in a terminal: a launch prompt, an orchestration dispatch, an issue or task prompt, or `orca terminal send` to an agent. A prompt a person submits is never hooked, and writes to one terminal stay in order while it decides. Rewrite `prompt` with `next`, or return `{ deny }` to refuse it.
  event `{ agent: string | null; terminalId: string; prompt: string; inputKind: "driving" | "orchestration" | "launch" }`; `next` may change `prompt`; stop with `{ deny: string }`
- `agent.tool.before` (since 1.4.248): An agent in an Orca terminal is about to run a tool. Claude Code waits for the answer: return `{ deny }` to refuse the call (the agent sees the reason) or change `input` with `next`; the person is still asked as usual. Other agents only report the call, so their results are ignored. Agents on SSH or WSL hosts are not hooked yet.
  event `{ agent: string; workspaceId: string | null; terminalId?: string; tool: string; input: JSON; callId?: string }`; `next` may change `input`; stop with `{ deny: string }`
- `agent.tool.after` (since 1.4.248): An agent in an Orca terminal finished a tool call (successfully or not). Observe only: Orca does not wait for it.
  event `{ agent: string; workspaceId: string | null; terminalId?: string; tool: string; input: JSON; callId?: string; output?: JSON }`; `next` may change nothing; stop with nothing (observe only)
- `editor.save.before` (since 1.4.248): The person is about to save a text file from an Orca editor tab (an explicit save, not autosave). Change `text` with `next` (format on save) or return `{ deny }` to refuse the save, which shows your reason. Edits made while the hook ran stay unsaved.
  event `{ workspaceId: string | null; path: string; languageId?: string; text: string }`; `next` may change `text`; stop with `{ deny: string }`

## Capabilities

- `workspace:read` (since 1.4.160): Read your projects and workspaces (names, branches, paths and agent status) and the terminals in them, and get notified when they change
- `workspace:write` (since 1.4.248): Open and rename your workspaces, focus their terminals, open their files in Orca, and run its built-in commands
- `agent:read` (since 1.4.245): Get notified when agent status changes
- `agent:launch` (since 1.4.248): Start and resume agents in your workspaces, local and SSH
- `terminal:send` (since 1.4.160): Open terminals, close the ones it opened or that are in your focused workspace, and type and run commands in your terminals, local and SSH
- `terminal:read` (since 1.4.248): Read the output of your terminals, local and SSH
- `notifications:show` (since 1.4.160): Show desktop notifications labeled with the plugin name
- `storage:own` (since 1.4.245): Store data in the plugin's own storage folder
- `secrets:own` (since 1.4.245): Store and read secrets in the plugin's own encrypted file
- `settings:own` (since 1.4.160): Read and change the plugin's own settings
- `appearance:write` (since 1.4.249): Publish and select desktop application, editor and terminal colors
- `workspace:create` (since 1.4.258): Create workspaces (new Git branches and worktrees) in your projects, local and SSH; a project's setup script runs as its settings say
- `automation:read` (since 1.4.258): Read your automations: their names, prompts, agents, projects, workspaces and schedules
- `automation:write` (since 1.4.258): Create automations that start agents in your projects on a schedule, even when the plugin is not running, and change or delete them (Orca asks you first for ones the plugin did not create, and before it changes what one with extra agent settings runs)
- `history:read` (since 1.4.258): Read the list of your past agent sessions on this computer, from the history files of the coding agents Orca supports, including running WSL distributions on Windows (not SSH or other machines, Antigravity IDE conversations or subagent transcripts): each session's title, which is often the start of its first message, agent, workspace, branch, times, and message and token counts; never the conversation itself

## Errors

A failed call rejects with an `Error` carrying `code`, `message`, `retryable` and, for `rate_limited`, `retryAfterMs`. Treat an unknown code as `action_failed`.

- `invalid_request`: the call itself is malformed
- `invalid_params`: params do not match the method, including a field this Orca does not know; the message names it
- `unknown_method`: the method does not exist in this Orca
- `capability_denied`: the manifest does not declare the capability
- `consent_required`: the plugin is disabled or the user has not approved this version
- `not_permitted`: the method or document is not available here, e.g. a worker-only method from a panel
- `rate_limited`: calls arrive faster than the budget; `retryAfterMs` says when to try again
- `unavailable`: the service behind the method is not running yet
- `action_failed`: the method ran and failed
- `cancelled`: the caller aborted the call through its `signal`
- `timeout`: Orca gave up waiting
- `conflict`: the call was made against a stale version, e.g. an editor edit after an outside change
- `too_large`: the message is larger than Orca accepts
